findings: ExtractTaskID emitted lowercase fz-2247, splitting new Git evidence from the uppercase Jira FZ-2247 row and making the exact commits API miss it.
Canonicalizing directly onto the Jira row initially exposed a second defect: Git authors could overwrite the Jira assignee and make the Work Item disappear under core-member visibility.
The push handler only checked the branch and last commit; a Jira key carried by an earlier commit in the same crane_manager batch could be missed.
The open CommitTelemetryPanel fetched once and did not consume application SSE updates.
Current database evidence has task_executor webhook delivery for FZ-2247 but no crane_manager webhook delivery at all, even though the repository is configured.

decisions: Unify Daily Jira through the existing Phase 41 tokens, 16/20px radius scale, matte structural panels, and table/inspector geometry; do not copy DecisionDashboard metric-card theater or introduce a second component system.

At stacked breakpoints derive the table panel height from the visible row count within a 320-560px cap; at CSS widths up to 760px hide project and recent-activity columns so the table fits without document horizontal overflow.
Use non-overlapping natural-day cohorts: age 0, age 3-6, and age 7+; keep age 1-2 as a watch count outside the requested checkpoints.
Persist daily Jira follow-up, escalation, and reassignment as DecisionEvent plus legacy DecisionLogs; only reassignment changes LastUpdate and invokes Jira assignee sync.
Keep Daily Jira as one flat table with an inline inspector; shell owns the submenu and App owns decision-view breadcrumbs.
Use shared Select for demand difficulty to inherit the verified selection, dismissal, keyboard, and adaptive-placement contract.
Scope task-detail color correction to .task-detail-surface at the end of TaskKanban styles rather than changing shared Modal or the dark task board.
Treat TaskTelemetry due_date as the shared source of truth for decision and schedule; reject no-op reschedules instead of recording misleading success events.
Preserve automatic-decision dates at the API boundary with occurred_at; keep the old time field only for compatibility.
Place automatic flow and meeting interventions in one main-panel event timeline because they form one operational chronology; preserve distinct markers and evidence links.
Implement vertical overlay placement in shared Select and DatePicker primitives so all consuming pages inherit the behavior.
Treat the Phase 41 redesign as product UI: SPECTACLE=2, DENSITY=8, light management workspace, table-first, inspector-backed, and evidence-first.
Add the coded prototype before full migration because existing Svelte pages are large and business-critical.
Gate the prototype behind `config:read` rather than replacing decision/schedule/evidence/settings pages.
Keep the prototype centered on exception, schedule, evidence, and override workflows, not a generic queue or broad cockpit.
Use the Phase 41 token substrate and `contract.ts` shapes as the foundation for production page migration.
Use a table-first command surface and right-side inspector as the core production-page interaction.
Use grouped submenus when a page has multiple configuration/security subareas, but render those submenus in the global shell rail/menu rather than inside the page content frame.
Keep the right content area structurally unified: breadcrumb navigation above, actual business content below.

Do not render `FunctionalWorkspace`'s context bar by default on production pages; the topbar is the page identity layer and content should begin with metrics, compact controls, tables, and inspectors.
Require a recorded Impeccable + design-taste-frontend + finesse-ui consensus before frontend edits, then run Impeccable detection and authenticated browser validation after implementation.
Preserve child configuration components during Settings shell migration so real save/test/RBAC/audit flows keep working.
Use `/prototype.html` for no-login visual review and the authenticated app route for real production functionality.
Let the left Settings configuration surface determine desktop row height; absolutely contain the audit panel so long diffs cannot inflate both columns.
Treat the new-demand and AI pre-deconstruction dialogs as one centered desktop group with a 16px gap and measured equal height.
Keep demand title and description as separate UI fields and serialize them into labeled LLM prompt sections instead of concatenating unmarked text.
Keep demand search inside the association dropdown so operators can filter and select without leaving the current AI workflow.
Stream human-readable Markdown before a fixed delimiter and structured JSON after it; display the Markdown live while retaining the JSON as the governed persistence model.
Emit stream completion only after both the demand spec and default review contract commit successfully.
Treat Markdown as the canonical editable document surface while retaining structured specification fields as progressively disclosed execution metadata.
Use one bounded CodeMirror workbench boundary and hairline-separated sections instead of delivery-stage or preview cards nested inside the detail modal.
Keep persisted demand specifications preview-only at rest; use double-click direct manipulation for editing and commit changed Markdown when the pointer moves outside the workbench.
Use a 960px demand-detail maximum and a two-group reviewer/policy contract rather than equal three-column form density.
Keep KPI as a top-level metric surface only; Settings route metadata must not expose a duplicate KPI configuration page.
Use glass only for Settings structural chrome, primary workbench, audit inspector, and overlays; keep inner facts, forms, tables, and permission branches flat with hairlines.
Centralize Settings section labels, permissions, fallback order, and navigation metadata in web/src/lib/settings-sections.ts.
